visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a medium shot of a man in a blue hoodie and jeans running with a stiff, unnatural posture on a residential street with apartment buildings in the background. News-style graphics with the label 'HAHA NEWS' and a QR code are overlaid at the bottom. (2) A transition leads to a street interview where a person with short black hair and glasses gestures emphatically while speaking into a microphone with a yellow 'HahaTai' logo. A white car and green trash cans are visible in the background. (3) A different man in a white sports shirt is interviewed on the street; he first demonstrates a normal running posture and then switches to a stiff-armed, weird run. (4) The scene shifts to a studio setting where a woman in a pink blazer and white necklace acts as a news anchor. She holds up a series of white boards with large Chinese characters written on them, pointing at them with a stick. (5) A man with messy hair, sunglasses, and a green shirt suddenly enters the studio frame, shouting and gesturing aggressively toward the anchor. (6) The final phase takes place in a cinema lobby with red lighting. The running man, now with messy face makeup, is seen with the sunglasses-wearing character. A movie poster with a child running in the dark is prominently displayed on the screen.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a high-energy male narrator delivering a news report over a fast-paced electronic BGM with a strong percussive beat. (2) A digital 'whoosh' transition leads to a female voice on the street, speaking with a high arousal, complaining tone. (3) A male voice enters with a conversational tone, demonstrating a 'normal' running rhythm before switching to a joking delivery. (4) A bell 'ding' SFX marks the start of the studio segment, where a female anchor speaks in an exaggerated, authoritative news tone. (5) A loud, aggressive male voice suddenly interrupts with high vocal tension and shouting, accompanied by a cartoonish 'thud' sound effect. (6) The final phase features a mix of the aggressive male voice and the narrator, closing with a dramatic movie stinger SFX and a final promotional tagline.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Montage: Hook -> News Parody -> Street Reactions -> Absurdist Analysis -> Reveal/CTA
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: This video is a creative parody of a sensationalist news broadcast designed to promote the horror/mystery movie 'Mebrouk' (Chinese title '凶器'). It uses the 'social news' format typical of the channel HahaTai to build awareness of the movie's central gimmick (the weird running) through absurdist humor and street interviews.

endorsement_analysis.endorsementCues: Display of the movie poster, release date 8/14, and direct call to action to see 'Mebrouk' (凶器) in theaters.

high_inference.freeDescribe: The video utilizes a viral 'weird run' challenge aesthetic to create social media engagement for a traditional film release. High editing density and familiar TV news tropes enhance the comedic effect.
